title: An Account of the Manners and Customs of the Modern Egyptians
author: Edward William Lane
notes: Project Gutenberg #70796; complete with transcriber's corrections list. First edition 1836 (Gutenberg text is a later standard edition of the same work). Covers domestic life, law, religion, customs. Second Afro-Asiatic entry alongside the Rwala Bedouin.

title: The Life of a South African Tribe (2 vols: I The Social Life; II The Psychic Life)
author: Henri A. Junod
notes: Vol 1 ~182k words, vol 2 ~210k words (vol 2 has the general index): https://archive.org/download/lifeofsouthafric02junouoft/lifeofsouthafric02junouoft_djvu.txt. Both volumes open in full, title page to end matter; OCR readable.

title: The Nandi: Their Language and Folk-Lore
author: A. C. Hollis
notes: Complete with index; OCR readable (some noise on plates). Book is mixed: Part I ethnography (social organisation, customs, religion; roughly a third of the book, well above 30k words), Part II grammar, Part III folk-lore. Flag: not purely ethnographic.

title: Tsuni-||Goam: The Supreme Being of the Khoi-Khoi
author: Theophilus Hahn
notes: Google scan; complete to 'THE END' and printer's imprint; OCR readable. Flag: centred on religion and mythology with comparative-philological argument, less on kinship and law; no fuller English monograph found online (Kolben 1731 English translation not located on IA or Gutenberg). Avoid the noisier copy tsuni-goam-the-supreme-being-of-the-khoi-khoi-theophilus-hahn.

title: The Todas
author: W. H. R. Rivers
notes: Complete with index and genealogical tables; OCR readable.

title: The Bontoc Igorot
author: Albert Ernest Jenks
notes: Project Gutenberg #3308; complete (letter of transmittal to final language notes, Gutenberg end marker). IA Google scan also complete: https://archive.org/download/bontocigorot00jenkgoog/bontocigorot00jenkgoog_djvu.txt. Ethnological Survey Publications vol. 1 (Manila). Distinct from the excluded Ifugao.

title: The Angami Nagas, with Some Notes on Neighbouring Tribes
author: J. H. Hutton
notes: Complete with index and printer's imprint; OCR readable.

other_names: Tai Long; Shans of Burma and Yunnan
title: Shans at Home, with two chapters on Shan history and literature
author: Leslie Milne (with W. W. Cochrane)
notes: Complete with index; OCR readable. Distinct from the excluded Central Thai. Two chapters on history and literature are by Cochrane; the rest describes Shan family life, customs and religion.

title: The Ainu and Their Folk-Lore
author: John Batchelor
notes: Complete, 39 chapters plus index; OCR readable. Covers customs, social life and religion as well as folk-lore.

title: The Mundas and Their Country
author: Sarat Chandra Roy
notes: Digital Library of India scan; complete from title page through final appendix; OCR readable. Large historical section precedes the ethnographic chapters.

other_names: Orokaiva of the Northern Division, Papua
title: Orokaiva Magic
author: F. E. Williams
notes: IA scan (digitized 2024) of the 1928 Oxford edition; full text opened publicly; complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: topical (cults, magic, ceremonies) rather than a general account; Williams' general 'Orokaiva Society' is 1930, too late.

title: The Natives of Mailu: Preliminary Results of the Robert Mond Research Work in British New Guinea (Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 39: 494-706)
author: Bronislaw Malinowski
notes: Digital Library of India scan of the whole journal volume (~340k words). The monograph runs from the heading 'The Natives of Mailu' (about character 1,145,600) to the start of S. A. White's 'Scientific Notes on an Expedition' (about character 1,668,400): ~90k words, complete with plate list. OCR readable. Not the excluded Trobriands.

title: The Euahlayi Tribe: A Study of Aboriginal Life in Australia
author: K. Langloh Parker
notes: Project Gutenberg #3819; complete through the glossary, Gutenberg end marker. IA Google scan also complete (~59k tokens incl. index): https://archive.org/download/euahlayitribewi00langgoog/euahlayitribewi00langgoog_djvu.txt.

family: Fuyug (isolate in Glottolog; no Goilalan family)
title: The Mafulu Mountain People of British New Guinea
author: Robert W. Williamson
notes: Complete with index and printer's imprint; OCR readable.

other_names: Murray Islanders; Mer; Miriam; Eastern Islanders (Mer, Erub, Ugar)
title: Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, Vol. VI: Sociology, Magic and Religion of the Eastern Islanders
author: A. C. Haddon (ed.), with W. H. R. Rivers, C. G. Seligmann, A. Wilkin and others
notes: IA metadata date says 1901 (series start) but the title page reads Volume VI, Cambridge University Press 1908. Complete volume; OCR readable. Multi-author report, but one society.

other_names: Gaigwu; Kiowa of the southern Plains
title: Calendar History of the Kiowa Indians (17th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 1, pp. 129-444)
author: James Mooney
notes: Project Gutenberg #46479; complete through index and Gutenberg end marker. Flag: weak fit, mainly tribal history and the pictographic calendars, with shorter sections on social organisation, the Sun Dance and customs; kept because no other pre-1929 Kiowa-Tanoan monograph was found online (Parsons 1925 Jemez and 1929 Tewa not located / too late).

title: The Thompson Indians of British Columbia (Jesup North Pacific Expedition vol. I, part 4; Memoirs of the AMNH vol. II)
author: James Teit (ed. Franz Boas)
notes: The file is the whole Jesup vol. I (1898-1900, ~225k words, with index); Teit's monograph runs from about character 466,000 to 1,060,000 of the file (running head 'THE THOMPSON INDIANS OF BRITISH COLUMBIA'), roughly 100k words, complete. OCR readable apart from noisy cover pages. Other parts of the volume (Smith archaeology, Boas facial paintings, Farrand basketry) are not part of the ethnography.

language: Tohono O'odham (toho1245; Glottolog's O'odham language incl. Akimel O'odham)
title: The Pima Indians (26th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, accompanying paper)
author: Frank Russell
notes: Google scan of the separately bound paper; runs through the final plates; no index in this scan (the report index is in the full volume). OCR readable. Distinct from the excluded Hopi and Tarahumara.

title: The Seri Indians (17th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, Part 1)
author: W J McGee (with J. N. B. Hewitt, Comparative Lexicology of Seri)
notes: Google scan of Part 1 of the report; complete through Hewitt's lexicology appendix; OCR readable.

title: The Omaha Tribe (27th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology)
author: Alice C. Fletcher and Francis La Flesche
notes: Complete annual report volume (the monograph is the whole report apart from the administrative front matter), through index; OCR readable.

title: Tsimshian Mythology (31st Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology)
author: Franz Boas (texts recorded by Henry W. Tate)
notes: Complete annual report volume through index (~554k tokens); OCR readable apart from cover noise. Flag: weak fit, mainly myths and comparative study; includes Boas's long 'Description of the Tsimshian, based on their mythology' (social organisation, customs, religion). No dedicated pre-1929 Tsimshian ethnography found online.

title: The Russian Peasantry: Their Agrarian Condition, Social Life, and Religion
author: Stepniak (S. M. Kravchinsky)
notes: Google scan; complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: a social and political study by a Russian emigre rather than fieldwork ethnography, but covers the village commune, family, customs and religion/sects. Included for European coverage in place of Robertson's Kafirs of the Hindu-Kush (Indo-European limit of 2).

language: Halh Mongolian (halh1238) and Inner Mongolian varieties
title: Among the Mongols
author: James Gilmour
notes: Digital Library of India scan of the Religious Tract Society edition (IA date 1888; first published 1883); complete from title page and prefatory note to the printer's imprint; OCR readable. Flag: missionary account mixing travel episodes with chapters on tents, food, lamas, religion, medicine and customs.

title: Life and Culture of the Hupa (University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 1(1))
author: Pliny Earle Goddard
notes: Google scan; complete (88 pp. plus plates and series list); OCR readable. Flag: short, close to the 30k-word floor (~35k words of text after boilerplate).

title: Ethnology of the Yuchi Indians (Anthropological Publications of the University Museum, University of Pennsylvania, vol. 1, no. 1)
author: Frank G. Speck
notes: Complete through the plates; OCR readable. Avoid ethnologyofyuchi00specuoft (bound with other papers, ~180k words).

title: The Maya Indians of Southern Yucatan and Northern British Honduras (BAE Bulletin 64)
author: Thomas W. F. Gann
notes: Library of Congress scan; complete with index; OCR readable (noise only on covers). Distinct from the excluded Tzeltal. title: The Zuñi Indians: Their Mythology, Esoteric Fraternities, and Ceremonies (23rd Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology)
author: Matilda Coxe Stevenson
notes: IA date 1905 (report for 1901-02, printed 1904). Complete volume through index; OCR readable. Strong on religion and ceremonies; also covers social customs, sociology and arts.

title: The Shasta (Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 17(5))
author: Roland B. Dixon
notes: Complete paper (pp. 381-498 with plates); OCR readable. Flag: short, near the 30k-word floor. Neighbours of the excluded Klamath but a different people and language family.

title: The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians (Report of the U.S. National Museum for 1895)
author: Franz Boas
notes: Separately bound extract; complete through the list of illustrations; OCR readable (includes Kwakwala texts and songs).

title: Indian Tribes of the Lower Mississippi Valley and Adjacent Coast of the Gulf of Mexico (BAE Bulletin 43)
author: John R. Swanton
notes: Google scan; complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: covers several tribes and is reconstructed mainly from 18th-century French sources; the Natchez account is the core and largest part (well over 30k words).
